expected.summary: Tides are the rise and fall of sea levels caused by the gravity of the Moon and the Sun [1]. The gravity of the Moon causes two tidal bulges on opposite sides of the Earth [2]. Spring tides occur when the Sun, Moon and Earth are in a line [3].

input: How do vaccines train the immune system?

expected.summary: Vaccines train the immune system to recognize a germ without causing the disease [1]. After vaccination, B cells make antibodies that bind to the germ [2]. A vaccine gives active acquired immunity to a particular disease [4]. Vaccines create long-lived memory B cells and T cells [5]. Some vaccines use mRNA to give cells instructions to make a harmless piece of a viral protein [6].

A black hole is a region of space where gravity is so strong that not even light can escape [1]. Black holes form when very massive stars collapse at the end of their life [4]. Detectors observed gravitational waves from two merging black holes [6]. Most large galaxies have a supermassive black hole at their center [7].

Honeybees perform a waggle dance to tell other bees the direction and distance to food [1]. The angle of the waggle run shows the direction of the food relative to the sun [4]. Bees release pheromones to signal alarm and to mark the hive [2]. Worker bees also use vibration signals to change the activity of other workers [6].

CRISPR is a gene editing technology that lets scientists change DNA at a chosen location [1]. CRISPR sequences were first found in bacteria as part of an immune defense against viruses [2]. The Cas9 enzyme cuts DNA at a site that a guide RNA selects [4]. Research shows that Cas9 can be programmed with RNA to cut specific DNA sequences [5]. One risk is unwanted cuts at DNA sites that are similar to the target site [7].
